tagline.text: A May flower festival in San Pedro, Laguna, working to revive the national flower

location.label: Location
location.text: San Pedro City, Laguna (around City Hall and the Sampaguita Park and Nursery)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱300–1,500 (day trip from Manila, per person)

children.text: The San Pedro Sampaguita Festival is held by San Pedro, Laguna, once a leading source of the national flower, to revive its flower industry. In recent years it has run in late May with garden and flower-arrangement contests, dancing, pageants and music shows.

The sampaguita is the national flower of the Philippines, known for the strong fragrance of its small white blossoms. In the Philippines, garlands of these flowers are placed around the necks of honored guests and at graduations and religious events. San Pedro City in Laguna is known as a city of this flower. Local press has carried recollections that travelers coming south from Manila could smell sampaguita as they entered San Pedro, and the city was once regarded as the main supplier of sampaguita in the Luzon area. According to local press reports, Barangay Nueva was known for trading sampaguita buds that were strung into garlands and necklaces, while Barangays San Vicente and Magsaysay had large plantations that supplied those traders. The mayor says the trade was popularized by a man named David Amante after World War II and was for a long time a main source of income for many residents.

The San Pedro Sampaguita Festival is a city festival built around this flower. According to local press reports, it was suspended for a time by COVID-19 and returned in 2023. At the relaunch on May 1, 2023, the city opened a sampaguita nursery and park, and the mayor called the festival a launchpad for economic recovery after the pandemic. The festival is said to focus on showcasing the many products made from the national flower. It continued in 2024 and 2025, and the 2025 edition was held in May. The city also takes pride in having entered the Guinness World Records in February 2009 for the longest sampaguita garland, measuring
3.6 km

For a traveler, this festival is less a major tourist event than an occasion when a local community tends the city's identity again. The 2025 edition ran from May 22 to 25 under the theme Mabighani sa Samyo ng Sampaguita, roughly meaning enchanted by the fragrance of sampaguita. The program included a dance contest, a pageant for young men and women, music shows and flower contests. It is not large, but you can mingle closely with local people, and it is easy to do as a day trip from Manila.

This guide is based on reports from recent years. The dates and program have changed from year to year, and one report says the 2026 edition was scaled down because of the energy crisis. Some sources say the festival is held in February or March, so the timing seems to have moved around. Before you go, be sure to check the latest announcements from the San Pedro city government and the official Sampaguita Festival Facebook page.

Named the highlight of the 2025 festival, this contest was a first attempt in which eight barangays and homeowners' associations set aside land to plant sampaguita and build gardens. The city plans to expand the program to grow more sampaguita.

A contest of centerpieces and installations made from the flowers, held in 2025 on May 24 at Robinsons Galleria South. It grew out of a garland competition held the year before, which was well received.
A dance event held on May 22, the first day of the 2025 festival. It was scheduled as the opening act, and you should check each year's notices for participating groups and venue.

blocks.title: Ginoo at Binibining San Pedro pageant

children.text: The pageant held on May 23 selects a young man and woman to represent the city. It is the kind of event often seen at Philippine local festivals.
A music concert held on May 24. The 2025 schedule listed it on the same day as the creative competition. Check the notices for the lineup and venue.
A sampaguita park and nursery of about
in Barangay Rosario, opened during the 2023 festival. It is reported to hand out seedlings free of charge to residents who want to plant sampaguita.
On May 25, the last day of 2025, a pet event called the Sampaguita Petstival and an American Bully show were held. It is a family-friendly event that borrows the sampaguita name.

blocks.title: Reading the rise and fall of the sampaguita industry

children.text: Throughout the festival you can see how the city's industry has changed. As housing and industrial development grew from the 1980s, the planted area fell from about 30 hectares in the 1990s to about 3 hectares in 2016 and then below 1 hectare, and dedicated growers fell from 20 to 3, according to the city agriculture office. Traders today bring in flowers from plantations in Central Luzon. So the festival can be read as a pleasant flower show and also as an attempt to win back a fragrance the city has lost.

items.title: Day trip from Manila
items.subtitle: Festival events and a visit to the Sampaguita Park

children.text: Head south from Manila or Alabang on SLEX to San Pedro. It takes about
1 hour
without traffic but can take longer on weekends.
Check that day's program around City Hall and the official venue. The schedule is posted on the official Facebook page.
See the sampaguita garden competition or flower displays, and watch how sampaguita garlands are strung.
Have lunch at a restaurant in town. San Pedro is close to Manila, so both Filipino food and fast food are easy to find.
Look around the Sampaguita Park and Nursery in Barangay Rosario. Check the opening hours locally.
Catch an evening concert or pageant if there is one, and return to Manila before it gets late.
The event timetable changes every year. Treat this order as a guide and adjust it to local announcements.

At the city tourism, culture and arts office or an event information desk, check that year's program and which barangays are in the garden contest. Ask whether you can visit a few of the gardens on your schedule.
Around Barangay Nueva, look for vendors who string sampaguita garlands, watch the process, and buy a garland or two. Ask the price first.
At the Sampaguita Park and Nursery in Barangay Rosario, ask staff which varieties are grown and how, and learn about the seedlings the city gives out.
Have dinner in town, watch an evening show, and head home before traffic builds up.
Some places may not be open depending on the time of year. Check local announcements first.
The most common way is to take a Laguna-bound bus or UV van from a SLEX-bound terminal in Manila, Pasay or Alabang and get off in San Pedro. Routes and fares differ by operator, so check locally.
San Pedro sits just south of Muntinlupa at the southern edge of Metro Manila, about 29 km from Manila, so it is relatively close via SLEX.

San Pedro's PNR station closed when Alabang-Calamba trips stopped on 2 July 2023, and the Tutuban-Alabang section also stopped in March 2024 for North-South Commuter Railway (NSCR) construction, so you cannot get there by train now (no reopening date). Use a bus, UV or Grab.
Rail service information changes frequently. Check official announcements before you leave.
You can take SLEX by ride-hailing car such as Grab or by rental car. Downtown is crowded on festival days, so arrive early near City Hall and check parking.
Tricycles and jeepneys are convenient in town. If the distance between venues is short, you can also walk.

The Sampaguita Festival has been held in late May in recent years. Reports gave a May 1 relaunch event in 2023, May 22–25 in 2025, and a May 22 start in 2026. Some sources say it used to be held in February or March, so check each year.

May is when the hottest season ends and the rainy season begins in the Philippines. Days are hot and humid, and afternoon showers sometimes fall. Early morning and evening are more comfortable for outdoor events.

San Pedro is easy to visit in a day from Manila, so an overnight stay is usually unnecessary. If you need a night, nearby Laguna cities or hotels in Metro Manila offer more choices. Downtown traffic is congested on festival days, so start early if you want to avoid a late return. The mayor acknowledges that most land is zoned commercial, which makes it hard to bring back large plantations, and encourages residents and businesses to plant sampaguita in backyards, vacant lots or even pots. Knowing this context makes even a small garden contest more meaningful.

City restaurants, food courts and malls are fine for eating. Just as the 2025 creative competition was held at Robinsons Galleria South, large malls are sometimes used as venues, so they can serve as an air-conditioned place to rest. Check that street food looks hygienic before eating.
Major events are livestreamed and schedules posted on the official Sampaguita Festival Facebook page. Check it before you go.
The dates change every year, so check the city government's announcement in early May before booking flights and transport.
Midday heat in May is intense. Bring a hat, water and sunscreen.
SLEX south of Manila is congested on weekends and during events. An early start is recommended.
It is a small local festival, so go ready to mingle with residents rather than with big expectations.
Sampaguita garlands are a tradition given as gifts of welcome and thanks. If you buy one, keep it in a shaded, cool place.
The nursery was reported to give out sampaguita seedlings to residents. Ask locally whether visitors can receive them.
The festival dates and program change every year, and the scale can shrink because of circumstances such as the energy crisis, so check the city government's announcements just before you go.
Sampaguita plantations have shrunk greatly because of development. Do not expect to see large flower fields around the city.
Venues get crowded. Keep your belongings in front of you.
SLEX and downtown traffic can jam, so leave plenty of time for the return.
May has strong midday heat and afternoon showers. Bring an umbrella and water.
The Philippines' best-known amusement park, in Santa Rosa, Laguna, which you reach by continuing south along SLEX from San Pedro.
An old town on the Laguna de Bay side where Spanish-era buildings remain. It fits well as an extra day alongside the festival.
The largest of the seven lakes of San Pablo City, Laguna, a good place to rest at a lakeside restaurant.
